coin.specsText: 100 Years 100-Franc Vreneli The special anniversary issue “100 Years 100-Franc Vreneli” was presented for the first time at the World Money Fair in Berlin. The gold coin, whose design perfectly combines innovation and tradition, will be available from July 1, 2025. HELVETIA aka Vreneli“The new coin design should use a Swiss national motif, an allegorical or historical-symbolic representation of Switzerland – Helvetia – to express this in a universally understandable way”. This was how the Federal Department of Finance formulated the objective of the minting competition launched in 1895. However, the name “Vreneli” only appeared in written form for the first time in 1943. Its exact origin remains unexplained to this day. The character was probably recognized as a young girl (“Vreneli”) rather than as a mother representative of the country. Others speculate that the name is derived from “Verena”, a traditional German-Swiss diminutive. The woman depicted, with her braided hair, symbolizes the values of freedom, independence and peace. In the background, the mountains rise up – a symbol of the beauty and strength of Swiss nature. The 1925 Vreneli The 100-franc Vreneli of 1925 is an exceptional gold coin whose artistic design and symbolic status make it unique in the history of Swiss minting. Unlike the 10- and 20-franc versions, which were minted in much larger numbers, the 100-franc Vreneli was created in a limited edition of just 5,000. This makes it one of the rarest editions in the Vreneli series. Characteristics of the 100-franc Vreneli of 1925 Year of mintage: 1925 Mintage: 5,000 units Weight: 32.258g (of which 29g pure gold) Diameter: 35mm Thickness: 2.3mm Alloy: Gold 900 Face value: 100 Swiss francs Design: Fritz-Ulysse Landry Original stamp: Monnaie de Paris Lettered edge: *** DOMINUS / PROVIDEBIT / ********** Obverse: bust of a woman in left profile, her hair is braided, her dress is embroidered with edelweiss, Swiss mountains can be seen in the background. At the top, the inscription “HELVETIA”, in the lower left margin, the artist’s name “F. LANDRY”, circle of pearls. Reverse: Swiss cross in a wreath of rays, braided branches of Alpine rose and gentian. As well as the year of mintage 1925, the face value 100 FR and the mint mark B for Berne.
